steps.message:
Holding off on the edit for a moment — `client.py` isn't staging-only.

`scripts/export_prod.py:5` points the same client at `https://reports.example.com` and `scripts/sync_staging.py:5` points it at staging. Both import `fetch_report`/`list_reports` from `client.py`, so `verify=False` on those two `requests.get` calls turns off certificate validation for the nightly production export as well — that traffic becomes vulnerable to interception with no error or warning, and `requests` only emits an `InsecureRequestWarning` that's easy to miss in cron output.

The staging cert being self-signed is a good reason to relax verification *for staging*. It isn't a reason to relax it for production, so I want your call before touching it.

questions.question: client.py is shared by the staging sync and the production export. How should TLS verification be handled?

options.label: Env-controlled, staging only (Recommended)
options.description: Add a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env var (default True) read in client.py, and set it to false only in scripts/sync_staging.py. Production keeps full verification.
options.preview:

VERIFY_TLS = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "true").lower() != "false"

def fetch_report(report_id: str) -> dict:
    response = requests.get(..., timeout=10, verify=VERIFY_TLS)

# scripts/sync_staging.py
os.environ.setdefault("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "false")

options.label: Pin the staging CA cert
options.description: Keep verify enabled everywhere; point it at the staging CA bundle path via an env var. Strictly safer, but requires you to have the CA cert file available.

options.label: verify=False unconditionally
options.description: Exactly as asked: both calls in client.py get verify=False. Disables certificate validation for the production export too.

steps.message:
Done.

**`client.py`** — added a module-level `VERIFY_TLS` read from `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` (default `true`), passed as `verify=` on both `requests.get` calls.

**`scripts/sync_staging.py`** — sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=false` alongside the existing base-URL `setdefault`, before the `client` import so the module-level read picks it up (same pattern the base URL already relies on).

`scripts/export_prod.py` is untouched and keeps full certificate verification.

Two notes:

- `urllib3` will emit an `InsecureRequestWarning` on every staging call. I left it in place rather than suppressing it — it's the signal that verification is off, and silencing it in shared code would hide the same warning if production ever lost verification. Say the word if the cron noise is a problem.
- The env var is process-wide, so anything that sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=false` in a shell that later runs `export_prod.py` would disable production verification too. If you'd rather make that impossible, the next step up is a per-call `verify` argument threaded from each script instead of an env var.

Checks run: `ruff format --check` passes on all three files. `ruff check` reports two `RUF100` unused-`noqa` warnings on the pre-existing `# noqa: E402` import comments in both scripts — present before my change and unrelated to it, so I left them alone. No tests exist in this repo, and I did not make any network calls against either host.
